sentences.text: Devilal S/o Shri Ambalal, Aged About 54 Years, R/o Village Saldari, P.s. Baghpura, Tehsil Jhadol, Dist. Udaipur,raj.

(Presently Lodged In Central Jail, Udaipur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through PP  ----Respondent  Connected With  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 11598/2024 Lokesh S/o Navla, Aged About 33 Years, R/o Ker Phala, Village Undari Kala P.s. Nai, Dist. Udaipur,raj.
(Presently Lodged In Udaipur Jail)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through PP  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Love Jain  Mr. Pritam Joshi For Respondent(s) : Mr. Prem Singh Panwar, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 12/11/2024

These applications for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) has been filed by the petitioners who have been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.200/2023, registered at Police Station Nai, District Udaipur, for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468,
471 & 120-B of IPC.

As per the prosecution, the allegation against the present petitioners is that the petitioner- Lokesh being the broker and the petitioner- Devilal being the witness to the sale, got an agreement to sale executed and registered for the sale of a land situated in Sindhu Ghati between the complainant party being the buyers and the co- [2024:RJ-JD:45723] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-11596/2024] accused Devilal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45723) on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100448463/
1 persons namely Smt. Sovani Bai and Smt. Lilki Bai being the sellers of the property in question.

As per the FIR, the complainant Shri Homa later on found out that they neither were the real owners of the land nor they were having possession over the said piece of land and were merely impersonating the real owners of the land in question.
Learned counsel contended that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel submitted that whatever the offences so alleged to have been committed in the present case have been committed by the above named co-accused persons only as the petitioners were never informed of the fact that the co-accused persons were not the real owners of the piece of land which has been sold to the complainant illegally.

Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the offences alleged to have been committed by the petitioners are triable by magistrate; the petitioners are in judicial custody;
investigation against them has already been completed; challan has been filed before the competent criminal Court and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time
, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioners.
Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and particularly the fact that specific allegations has been levelled by the complainant mainly against the above named co-accused persons; investigation against the [2024:RJ-JD:45723] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-11596/2024]
petitioners have already been completed; the offences alleged to have been committed by the petitioners are triable by Magistrate and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the material prosecution witnesses of the case or fleeing away from justice or tampering with the evidence, in case he is enlarged on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. (483 BNSS) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioners Devilal S/o Shri Ambalal and Lokesh S/o Navla arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.200/2023, registered at Police Station Nai, District Udaipur, shall be released on bail,
if not wanted in any other case, provided each of them furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for their appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
A copy of this order be placed in each file.
